prs.title: fix(streamable-http): wait for post_writer before yielding
prs.author: Epochex
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Race condition in streamable_http.py's post_writer: the caller (the streamablehttp_client context manager) starts post_writer as a fire-and-forget task and yields the read/write streams to the caller before post_writer has actually entered its stream context and is ready to consume writes, so a message sent immediately after yield can be missed/lost. Both PRs fix this identically: add a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter to `post_writer` and call `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the stream context manager(s), so the caller can use `tg.start(post_writer, ...)` and block until post_writer signals readiness before yielding. (2 PRs)

members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov

members.title: Race condition in streamable http
members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: Race condition in streamable_http.py's post_writer: the caller (the streamablehttp_client context manager) starts post_writer as a fire-and-forget task and yields the read/write streams to the caller before post_writer has actually entered its stream context and is ready to consume writes, so a message sent immediately after yield can be missed/lost. Both PRs fix this identically: add a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter to `post_writer` and call `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the stream context manager(s), so the caller can use `tg.start(post_writer, ...)` and block until post_writer signals readiness before yielding.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs modify the same RequestResponder.cancel() method in src/mcp/shared/session.py, branched from the identical parent blob (243eef5ae6), to change what happens when an in-flight request is cancelled. The pre-existing code in cancel() sent an ErrorData response back to the peer, which violates the spec rule that receivers must not send a response for a cancelled request. #2493 removes that response-send outright (and updates the corresponding comment/log in server.py's _handle_request cancelled-path from 'duplicate response suppressed' to the correct spec rationale, keeping both sides of the call path consistent). #2514 touches the same cancel() method and adds a CancelledNotificationParams import, indicating it replaces the same response-send with a notifications/cancelled emission instead - a different remedy for the identical code location and trigger. (2 PRs)
